messages:
leo-acme: Hey team, our onboarding smoke tests are getting 429s immediately once we ramp workers. Using node pool + SDK v1.2. Example: single API key, ~25 parallel workers.

maria-cs: Sorry for the hit, leo. Are the requests originating from the client (browser) or server? Any proxy in front?

leo-acme: Server-side lambda pool behind an internal proxy. We followed the server quickstart but left the example fanout code as-is.

jamie-eng: Probable short-window concurrency limiter. Server-side pools need lower concurrency than the browser examples imply. Try reducing concurrent requests to 3-5 and add randomized backoff.

nina-sre: I inspected the ingress metrics for acct "acme-enterprises" at 2139998780: a 30s spike to ~120 req/s from same source IP triggers our short-window guard. We can temporarily relax the limiter for your onboarding window if you need sustained throughput.

maria-cs: Two routes: 1) immediate mitigation: client-side concurrency cap + exponential retries with jitter; 2) short-term uplift: we can bump your per-minute quota for 4h for integration testing. Which do you want?

leo-acme: We'll try throttling first and re-run. Also, does switching to session tokens vs long-lived key change rate-limits?

jamie-eng: Use server keys and reuse connections. Do not refresh tokens per request. Session tokens are fine but avoid issuing a fresh token for every call since auth ops can also hit limits.

leo-acme: Quick test: limited to concurrency=4 + jitter, 429s stopped. Thanks.

quota-bot: Ticket CS-2210 created: "Acme integration throttle investigation". Assigned: nina-sre.

maria-cs: Great. I'll put a 30-min enablement to go over SDK patterns (connection reuse, concurrency, token handling) and add notes to the onboarding checklist. Leaving ticket open to monitor for 12h.

leo-acme: Appreciate the quick help :rocket:
